description: ICS Village brings together operators, researchers, and government leaders to address critical infrastructure defense, industrial control systems security, turbine controls, OT forensics, and active defense.

talks.title: 5 Quick Wins for Improving ICS Cybersecurity Posture
talks.teaser: Outlines five practical and high-impact security wins for strengthening industrial control system defenses.
talks.summary:
In this industrial cybersecurity briefing from the DEF CON Safe Mode ICS Village, principal industrial penetration tester Austin Scott presents five immediate, high-impact strategies for improving Operational Technology (OT) security posture. Opening at 00:02, Austin emphasizes practical security controls that can be implemented without disrupting continuous physical operations.

At 08:00, he stresses building collaborative relationships between enterprise security teams and plant operators to bridge cultural divides. At 16:01, he examines credential security, showing how client-side tools like SessionGopher extract saved credentials from jump boxes and highlighting the necessity of removing hardcoded administrative passwords.

At 24:01 and 32:00, Austin details endpoint hardening and passive network monitoring, demonstrating open-source tools like Sofia and NetworkMiner to establish asset inventories, baseline industrial protocol traffic, and detect anomalous communications across OT networks. talks.title: PowerLine Truck Hacking: 2TOOLS4PLC4TRUCKS
talks.teaser: Introduces two open tools for auditing and testing power-line communications and PLCs in heavy-duty vehicles.
talks.summary:
Automotive security researcher Ben Gardiner delivers a technical deep dive into heavy vehicle power line communications (PLC) in the ICS Village, introducing open-source hardware and software tools to assess commercial trailer network security [00:01, 00:06].

Gardiner explores SAE J2497 (PLC4TRUCKS), the standard that modulates multiplexed digital signals directly over existing 12V tractor-trailer power wiring to control pneumatic anti-lock braking systems (ABS) [08:35]. He details the development of modified "Truck Duck" hardware interfaces utilizing RF up-converters and software-defined radios to overcome bandwidth limitations [17:51, 26:56], analyzing regulatory considerations under FCC unintentional radiator exemptions [36:51] and demonstrating how unauthenticated PLC traffic can be injected to manipulate commercial trailer telemetry [45:41].

talks.title: Journey of ICS Project Files: Visibility and Forensics
talks.teaser: Explores parsing proprietary ICS engineering project files to gain deep forensic visibility into industrial controllers.
talks.summary:
In this technical reverse engineering session from the DEF CON Safe Mode ICS Village, a security researcher explores the forensic value and security risks of Industrial Control System (ICS) engineering project files. Opening at 00:00, the speaker introduces project files as rich repositories containing full plant architectures, PLC logic, I/O tag databases, and network topologies.

At 12:00, the presenter demonstrates how threat actors weaponize project files during reconnaissance to identify vulnerable controllers and map critical process tags prior to executing targeted physical disruption.

At 24:01 and 36:00, the talk dives into proprietary binary file formats, revealing how parser flaws and embedded database vulnerabilities in engineering workstations allow attackers to plant malicious payloads directly within project archives. Concluding at 48:00, the speaker urges defenders to treat ICS project files with the same scrutiny as executable macro files, establishing strict validation and sandboxing procedures before opening them on engineering stations. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Vulnerability Discovery: Tips for Surviving
talks.teaser: Shares practical survival tips and methodologies for researching and disclosing vulnerabilities in industrial systems.
talks.summary:
Claroty security researchers Doli Yardeni and Lemley present defensive lessons learned from discovering and remediating critical vulnerabilities in industrial control systems and operational technology networks in the ICS Village [00:01, 00:03].

The researchers examine industrial data historian architectures, showing how proprietary industrial network protocols interface with corporate business networks through web-based supervisory applications [04:51]. Using a case study of vulnerabilities in OSIsoft PI Web API systems [10:43], they demonstrate cross-site scripting (XSS) and server-side request injection risks, emphasizing rigorous Content Security Policy (CSP) implementation [19:35] and coordinated vulnerability disclosure with industrial automation vendors [23:54].

talks.title: Confessions of an Offensive ICS Researcher
talks.teaser: Reflects on years of offensive ICS research, physical process manipulation attacks, and defensive lessons learned.
talks.summary:
In this introspective presentation from the DEF CON Safe Mode ICS Village, a seasoned industrial penetration tester presents "Confessions of an Offensive ICS Researcher," detailing the transition from offensive vulnerability discovery to managing an enterprise cybersecurity program. Opening at 00:19, the speaker reflects on how offensive security mindsets often diverge from operational realities.

At 05:01, the presenter explains that while offensive researchers naturally focus on high-severity zero-day exploits, industrial defenders face complex operational constraints including regulatory compliance, patch validation, and 24/7 continuous uptime requirements.

Past 20:00 and 40:00, the talk explores real-world case studies of finding vulnerabilities in programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and supervisory systems. The speaker details the friction of coordinating disclosures with industrial hardware vendors and offers practical advice on translating red team findings into actionable, risk-prioritized engineering remediations. talks.title: MITRE ICS ATT&CK
talks.teaser: Introduces the MITRE ATT&CK for Industrial Control Systems knowledge base and its application to threat modeling.
talks.summary:
MITRE cyber security engineer Marie Otis introduces the MITRE ATT&CK for Industrial Control Systems (ICS) framework in the ICS Village, explaining how it models adversary behaviors targeting operational technology and physical engineering processes [00:00, 00:03].

Otis contrasts enterprise IT threat modeling with the physics-driven operational reality of industrial control networks, demonstrating how adversary objectives center on manipulating physical variables, disrupting safety systems, and altering device logic [04:52, 05:01]. She provides practical use cases for the framework, illustrating how asset owners use ATT&CK for ICS to conduct risk assessments, design realistic adversary emulation scenarios, map telemetry from proprietary PLC protocols, and structure tabletop incident response exercises [09:21, 14:00, 18:32].

talks.title: Operationalizing Cyber Norms
talks.teaser: Discusses operationalizing international cyber norms and rules of engagement to protect civilian critical infrastructure.
talks.summary:
In this international policy and security briefing from the DEF CON Safe Mode ICS Village, a reformed hacker and critical infrastructure specialist presents "Operationalizing Cyber Norms" live from Amsterdam. Opening at 00:00, the speaker explores how geopolitical tensions and state-sponsored cyber operations threaten civilian critical infrastructure.

At 02:01 and 03:00, the talk examines landmark international governance efforts, focusing on the 2015 United Nations Group of Governmental Experts (UN GGE) consensus report that established voluntary non-binding norms prohibiting cyberattacks against critical infrastructure.

At 04:00, the presenter references major historical incidents—including the 2012 Shamoon attacks against Saudi Aramco and attacks on power grids—to underscore the stakes. Concluding past 15:00, the speaker details how to operationalize diplomatic norms through regional CERT cooperation, mandatory incident transparency, and cross-border technical defense pacts. talks.title: Vivisecting PowerPC
talks.teaser: Demonstrates binary analysis and reverse engineering techniques targeting PowerPC firmware commonly found in industrial gear.
talks.summary:
In this ICS Village session, ac0rn and atlas 0f d00m demonstrate how to reverse engineer and disassemble PowerPC firmware using Vivisect, an open-source Python-based binary analysis and emulation framework originally developed by Invisigoth. The speakers explain that while x86 and ARM receive extensive tooling support, PowerPC architectures—widely deployed across industrial control systems, automotive engine control units (ECUs), aerospace systems, and NXP/Freescale platforms—often present distinct challenges for security analysts [05:35]. They highlight Vivisect's interactive IPython workflow, which enables rapid programmatic inspection, workspace modification, and custom disassembly extension [10:53].

The presentation explores the core mechanics of PowerPC instruction set architecture (ISA) decoding, including register conventions and control flow mechanisms [16:12]. The speakers detail the role of critical registers such as r1 for the stack pointer, r2 and r13 for Small Data Area (SDA) pointers, and r12 for indirect function calls [42:00]. They illustrate how firmware binaries handle function prologues, stack frame allocation, and return address management via link register manipulation (`mtlr` and `mflr`). Special focus is given to resolving indirect branches and switch jump tables, utilizing Vivisect's virtual address sets (VA sets) to map dynamic call targets and virtual method tables [47:08].

Through an interactive live demonstration, the authors walk through the manual identification and decoding of PowerPC instructions from raw firmware dumps and Volvo/automotive VBF containers [36:27]. They show how to spot reset vector entry points, identify code boundaries versus data sections, and build custom parsers to resolve ambiguous opcodes [52:30]. The session concludes with practical tips on navigating obscure embedded architectures and expanding automated analysis workflows within Vivisect.
